<reason>B won a competitive debate by turning CON’s “no stopping rule / unlimited descendants” attack into bounded design (defined awards, proof, survivor priority, one inherited claim) and making the decisive comparison whose interests close the window. A’s ratchet, privacy, and non-transmissible-claim points stayed live and original, but the irreversibility-as-reason-not-to-pay line was damaged, and the withheld-file/dying-survivor case left closed-chapter CON looking like a state-delay discount rather than a finished obligation.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 1–2: irreversibility does not justify less redress, plus “meaningful access” as a fair chance to prove (not an endless archive hunt), which then made CON’s dying-survivor closure look like rewarding delay rather than multiplying liability.</best_rebuttal>
